entries.name: Mexican Independence Day
entries.capsule: Marks the 1810 start of Mexico's war of independence; St. Paul's first Fiestas Patrias came in 1939.
entries.dateRule: September 16. Community events may fall on nearby days.
entries.whatItMarks: Start of the 1810 war of independence.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: St. Paul held its first Fiestas Patrias in 1939, with a parade from the West Side to downtown (MNopedia). A current dated celebration could not be confirmed. See also the Mexican page.

sources.title: Minnesotanos: Latino journeys in Minnesota, MNopedia

entries.name: Central American Independence Day
entries.capsule: Several Central American nations mark independence from Spain on this date, at the start of Heritage Month.
entries.dateRule: September 15.
entries.whatItMarks: Independence of Central America from Spain in 1821.

entries.name: Día de la Virgen de Guadalupe
entries.capsule: Feast honoring Our Lady of Guadalupe, kept in Minnesota with processions, Masses, mariachi and dance.
entries.dateRule: December 12. Some parishes begin the evening before.

dates.source: The Catholic Spirit: decree read on the feast day, December 12

entries.whatItMarks: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, tied to the reported appearance of the Virgin Mary to a Mexican peasant nearly five centuries ago.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: At the diocesan shrine in St. Paul, an annual one-mile procession, Mass and reception, with about 700 people at the anticipatory Mass in 2019. At Queen of Angels in Austin in 2019, Mass followed by a night of mariachi and chinelos dancers. In 2003 about 300 attended a midnight Mass at Misión El Santo Niño Jesús in St. Paul.

entries.name: Día de los Muertos
entries.capsule: Remembrance of the dead, honored in Minnesota with public celebrations, altars and art.
entries.dateRule: November 1 and 2. Public events may fall on nearby days.
entries.whatItMarks: Remembrance of the dead (observed November 1 and 2).
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: CLUES holds a public celebration at Midtown Global Market. Centro Tyrone Guzmán also promotes a 2026 celebration. The state council and Governor's Office recognized the day in 2025. Outside the Twin Cities, Mankato's Old Town festival closes four blocks of Riverfront Drive on the last Saturday of October; AP reported about 12,000 people on Oct. 25, 2025. In Minneapolis, more than 100 people followed Aztec dancers into El Colegio High School to see student altars on Nov. 1, 2025.

entries.name: Christmas
entries.capsule: Christian feast of the birth of Jesus.
entries.dateRule: December 25.
entries.whatItMarks: Birth of Jesus (Gregorian calendar).
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: At St. Paul's-San Pablo Lutheran in Minneapolis, members made paper flowers for pre-Christmas processions in the winter of 2025 to 2026 (Associated Press). No other Minnesota detail could be confirmed.

entries.name: Día de los Reyes
entries.capsule: The visit of the Magi, a gift day in many Latin American and Caribbean families.
entries.dateRule: January 6.
entries.whatItMarks: The visit of the Magi. Practice differs by family and by country of origin.

entries.name: Las Posadas (first night)
entries.capsule: Nine nights re-enacting Mary and Joseph's search for shelter, kept in some Latino Christian traditions.
entries.dateRule: December 16, for nine nights through December 24. Parish dates may vary.
entries.whatItMarks: Nine nights (December 16 to 24) re-enacting Mary and Joseph's search for shelter.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: No dated Minnesota Las Posadas could be confirmed. Pre-Christmas processions at St. Paul's-San Pablo Lutheran in Minneapolis were noted by the Associated Press in January 2026, without using that name.

entries.name: Hispanic Heritage Month (begins)
entries.capsule: U.S. month, September 15 to October 15, marked in Minnesota with festivals, art and business events.
entries.dateRule: Begins September 15 and ends October 15.
entries.whatItMarks: U.S. heritage month, September 15 to October 15, tied to Central American and Mexican independence days.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026: CLUES's group exhibition and Fiesta Latina, and Minneapolis's Latino Business Week. The state council and Governor's Office recognized the month in 2025. The University of Minnesota's Chicano & Latino Studies department also marks it, as Latinx Heritage Month. In 2026 the Hispanic Heritage Foundation held its 39th Hispanic Heritage Awards at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis on Sept. 10, the first time outside Washington, D.C., honoring 'the people of Minnesota.' Worthington High School's Sueños Club held a community fiesta on Oct. 2, 2026.

entries.name: Fiesta Latina
entries.capsule: CLUES's free family festival, held at CHS Field in St. Paul in 2026.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by CLUES.
entries.whatItMarks: A public celebration of Latino culture and community during Heritage Month.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Free and family-friendly, 11:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at CHS Field in 2026, the first year there. CLUES mentions plans for 2027.

minnesotaEvents.place: CHS Field, 360 N. Broadway St., St. Paul

entries.name: Cinco de Mayo on the West Side
entries.capsule: Two-day St. Paul street festival with a parade, music and food on the West Side.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by organizers, around May 5.
entries.whatItMarks: On the West Side, a yearly celebration of Mexican heritage and of the neighborhood, and in 2026 a hoped-for boost for businesses recovering from the enforcement surge.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Organized by the West Side Boosters Club and West Side Fiesta Committee, with car shows, more than 40 food vendors, 80 craft and service vendors, two stages, a kids zone and a parade. Attendance was roughly 30,000 the year before, per Sahan Journal.

minnesotaEvents.place: Cesar Chavez Street, West Side, St. Paul

entries.name: Latino Business Week
entries.capsule: Minneapolis week celebrating and supporting Latino-owned businesses, held for the third time in 2026.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the City of Minneapolis.

dates.source: City of Minneapolis news page (mayor's proclamation, Oct. 3 to 11); MPR News gave Oct. 5 to 11

entries.whatItMarks: Support for Latino-owned businesses, in 2026 during recovery from the enforcement surge.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Kickoff with Mayor Frey, a pop-up market on Historic Main Street and a celebration at Mercado Central, partly funded by city relief money.

minnesotaEvents.name: Latino Business Week 2026
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Proclaimed Oct. 3 to 11, 2026 by the city; MPR News reported Oct. 5 to 11

entries.name: Farmworkers Day
entries.capsule: Minnesota's governor proclaimed March 31, 2026, as Farmworkers Day after lawmakers repealed Cesar Chavez Day.
entries.dateRule: Proclaimed for March 31, 2026. No yearly law sets it, and no later proclamation was found.
entries.whatItMarks: The contributions of farmworkers and the sacrifices of immigrants and their families.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The governor's 2026 proclamation. West Side and school leaders spoke publicly that day, per FOX 9.

entries.name: Latine Day at the Capitol
entries.capsule: State council's annual gathering at the Capitol for Latino Minnesotans to meet lawmakers.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Minnesota Council on Latino Affairs during session.
entries.whatItMarks: Latino civic voice in state policy.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On April 24, 2025, under the theme Hope, Unity, and Action for a Better Future. A 2026 date could not be confirmed.

entries.name: Worthington International Festival
entries.capsule: Downtown Worthington festival with mariachi, Mexican dance, Afro-Peruvian and Ecuadorian acts alongside many other communities.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by organizers, in July.
entries.whatItMarks: Worthington's many cultures, begun in 1994 as a soccer tournament.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The 2026 schedule included Son de mi Tierra, Enlazados and Ecuador Manta. Earlier years featured Nuevo Guachinango, Los Vandettas, Salsa del Soul and Aztec dancers. It is a shared festival, not a Latino one alone.

minnesotaEvents.name: International Festival 2026
minnesotaEvents.place: Nobles County Government Center and downtown Worthington

sources.title: International Festival celebrates 30 years, The Globe

entries.name: Hispanic Heritage Awards (Minneapolis, 2026)
entries.capsule: National Latino awards held in Minneapolis in 2026, honoring Minnesotans' response to the enforcement surge.
entries.dateRule: Set by the Hispanic Heritage Foundation; usually opens Hispanic Heritage Month. Held in Minneapolis only in 2026 so far.
entries.whatItMarks: The 39th Hispanic Heritage Awards; its Humanitarian Award went to 'the people of Minnesota' for their response to Operation Metro Surge.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Ceremony at Orchestra Hall, Minneapolis, taped for a PBS broadcast; local nonprofits accepted the award.

entries.name: Old Town Mankato Day of the Dead
entries.capsule: Free daylong Day of the Dead street festival in Mankato's Old Town, among the largest in Minnesota.
entries.dateRule: Last Saturday of October, set by organizers each year.

dates.source: Minnesota State University, Mankato event listing (third party, not the organizer)

entries.whatItMarks: Day of the Dead remembrance with ofrendas, music, dance and lucha libre; begun by the Ek family at their paint business.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Four blocks of Riverfront Drive close to traffic; about 12,000 people attended on Oct. 25, 2025, per AP and KEYC.

entries.name: Willmar Cinco de Mayo
entries.capsule: Downtown Willmar street festival of Latino cultures hosted by the Latino Community Association of Willmar.
entries.dateRule: Set by the Latino Community Association of Willmar; held in mid-May in 2026.
entries.whatItMarks: Mexico's 1862 victory at Puebla, used in Willmar to celebrate many Latino cultures.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Games, music and food from Mexican, Guatemalan, Puerto Rican and other vendors on Fourth Street Southwest; more than 100 guests in 2026.

entries.name: Worthington Hispanic Heritage Community Fiesta
entries.capsule: Downtown Worthington fiesta for Hispanic Heritage Month, presented by the high school's Sueños Club.
entries.dateRule: Set by the organizers during Hispanic Heritage Month.
entries.whatItMarks: Hispanic Heritage Month.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Crafts, piñatas, food vendors, the band Son de mi Tierra and a DJ at the 10th Street Pavilion.
